paragraph: New Milford is a single-family town, with 47 detached home sales over six months against essentially no condo or co-op activity to speak of. The median came in at $715,000, the sale-to-list ratio was 1.025, roughly 62 percent of homes sold above asking, and the median days on market was 17. That is a real seller's market, and multiple offer situations are common on anything priced sensibly. Sales ranged from $365,000 to $1,675,000, so the median is the better guide than the spread. Most months here carry fewer than eight closings, too thin to read on their own, but July brought 18 sales at a median of $750,500, which is the normal summer peak. If New Milford follows the usual arc, expect closings and medians to ease through fall while competition on well-priced homes holds.
